title: Vector and Signal
premise: Mara Crane, the only courier still flying the silent corridor between the colony fleet Meridian and Earth's derelict relay stations, discovers that the colonies' children are dreaming the same dream: a voice counting down Earth's last transmission loop. The dream is a distress signal encoded in inherited memory, and Mara's own impossible-accident files are its key — her mother helped design the loop that will erase Earth's archives, and with them, the truth that the two fleets were separated by a lie. As hawks on both sides move to weaponize the countdown, Mara must keep the fleets believing the corridor is dead while smuggling the children's shared dream — and the confession it carries — between them. In the end she sacrifices her ship and her cover identity to broadcast the truth, and the fleets, bound by their children's shared dream rather than by treaties, begin to speak again.
about_author: Ines Pemberton is a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade listening to frequencies no one answered before turning to fiction. She writes from a converted lighthouse keeper's cottage on the northern coast, where she collects broken clocks.

chapters.title: The Long Quiet
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Flying the dead corridor between Meridian and Earth's relays, Mara logs another 'impossible accident' — a relay station that failed in a pattern too neat to be chance. The beat is loneliness sharpened into suspicion; she realizes someone is pruning the route she alone still flies.

chapters.title: Children of the Same Night
chapters.summary: Alternating Mara and colony teacher Dev Osei. Forty-seven children across three ships wake from an identical dream: a voice counting down. Dev reports it to Mara as a curiosity; she recognizes the countdown cadence from Earth's old transmission loops. Beat: wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Impossible Accidents
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Pulling her cold-case files, Mara finds every 'accident' on the corridor maps to a point where the loop's signal would have passed. Someone has been erasing Earth's voice for years. Beat: the investigator becomes the investigated, as her own file surfaces.

chapters.title: What Her Mother Built
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, with flashback chapters of letters. Mara learns her mother co-designed the transmission loop — and embedded a kill-switch that will wipe Earth's archives when the countdown ends. The inheritance theme lands: she has been carrying her mother's secret in her blood all along. Beat: grief and fury.

chapters.title: The Fleet That Doesn't Speak
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Meridian's council, tipped off about the dreams, declares the children's visions contagion and quarantines the young. Dev smuggles Mara the children's drawn dream-maps, which form a star chart pointing to a relay everyone believes destroyed. Beat: found family forming against authority.

chapters.title: Hawks
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Both fleets' intelligence services converge on Mara: Meridian wants the countdown silenced, Earth's remnant wants it broadcast to force reunion on their terms. Each offers her safety in exchange for the lie. Beat: the squeeze tightens; she chooses to deceive both.

chapters.title: The Relay at the End of the Map
chapters.summary: Mara and Dev's POV in alternation. A desperate run to the 'destroyed' relay with three of the dreaming children aboard, the dream acting as a living decryption key. They find the loop's heart — and a recording of Mara's mother confessing the separation was engineered. Beat: revelation as homecoming.

chapters.title: Keeping the Lie Alive
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Cornered by both fleets' warships at the relay, Mara broadcasts a false countdown extension, buying hours by pretending the loop still holds Earth's secrets hostage. The children, linked in sleep, begin answering the voice in the dream. Beat: defiance under impossible pressure.

chapters.title: Last Transmission Loop
chapters.summary: Climax, Mara's POV. The countdown ends for real; the archives begin to wipe. Mara burns her ship's core to hold the channel open and broadcasts her mother's confession — and the children's shared dream — to both fleets at once. Beat: sacrifice, identity dissolved into signal.

chapters.title: Vector and Signal
chapters.summary: Dev's POV, then Mara's, recovering aboard a Meridian hospital ship. The fleets, moved by their children's shared dream and the confession, open the corridor; Mara, stripped of her old name, is offered a new one by the families she made. Beat: quiet resolution — inheritance rewritten as a gift, not a debt.
